forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Horizon date 2026-05-22 and expires_at 2026-05-23 passed without formal collapse. US State Department did not withdraw ceasefire sponsorship — announced a fourth round of Israel-Lebanon talks June 2-3 in Washington and a Pentagon security-track meeting May 29. Lebanese government (President Aoun, Foreign Ministry) condemned Israeli violations but did not declare the truce void. IDF 'no ceasefire' rhetoric is a military framing, not a US government policy withdrawal. Ongoing IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate are consistent with the porous-truce pattern and do not meet the resolution bar. No Hezbollah barrage exceeded 50 launches per day. Resolution criteria unmet on both prongs.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown. Individual violations — which are continuous — do NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse (consistent with current porous-truce pattern). Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support.

forecasts.question: Will the US and Iran jointly announce a named Memorandum of Understanding (or equivalent written framework) — with public confirmation from both a named US official AND a named Iranian official — before EOD 2026-05-28?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial at 0.38 (Analyst), Judge-calibrated to 0.33. Trump May 23: 'largely negotiated,' 'announced soon.' US official May 24: 'coming days.' Washington Times May 23: announcement within 24h (did not materialize — expiration of that 24h window by May 24 compresses remaining timeline). Iranian principal silence (Araghchi, Pezeshkian) is the binding structural constraint for YES resolution. CBS May 25 'broad principles agreed including HEU disposal' is new positive evidence. Two NO paths within 72h: (a) Iranian side rejects wording; (b) Republican congressional blowback causes US delay.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official (Secretary of State, National Security Advisor, or Trump himself) AND a named Iranian principal (Araghchi or Pezeshkian) both publicly confirm a signed MOU or equivalent written framework before EOD 2026-05-28. Verbal 'agreement in principle' or one-sided confirmation does NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named principals from both sides; OR official State Dept press release AND Iran MFA press release issued within 72h of each other.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only US side confirms and Iran has not confirmed within 24h: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If envoys confirm but no principal-level statement within 72h: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If deal is announced but Khamenei's office disavows within 72h: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A signed document labeled 'MOU,' 'memorandum,' 'framework,' 'accord,' or any other named instrument resolves YES provided both US and Iranian principals publicly authenticate it — document title is NOT controlling; principal authentication IS controlling.

forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Netanyahu makes a formal Knesset speech or public announcement naming an election date earlier than 2026-10-27; OR if the Knesset passes a formal dissolution motion by majority vote. Leaks and media speculation do NOT resolve.

forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Coalition partner threatening dissolution without a formal Knesset vote = NOT resolved. Netanyahu 'considering' elections per aides = NOT resolved. Only a formal announcement by Netanyahu himself or a passed dissolution vote counts. The 110-0 preliminary reading on 2026-05-20 does NOT constitute dissolution — only a final third-reading majority vote of the Knesset passes into law and qualifies.

forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Revised 0.38→0.22. DA structural defect finding accepted: all May 22-24 transit data (33 ships May 24, 35 ships May 22) originates exclusively from IRGC and Iranian state media — none of the four qualifying independent sources (Lloyd's List, Windward, USNI News, UNCTAD). Independent sources confirmed approximately 2 vessels per day as of May 1 (USNI News). Conditional computation: p(Fd) = p(Fc=0.54) × p(Fd|Fc YES=0.20) + p(~Fc=0.46) × p(Fd|~Fc=0.05) = 0.108 + 0.023 = 0.131; Judge applies 0.22 as model-uncertainty-adjusted midpoint accounting for a faster-than-expected IRGC standdown scenario. The multi-step post-deal sequence (mines cleared + Lloyd's premium drop + major carrier return) within the 5-day window between June 5-10 is the binding constraint even conditional on Fc YES.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd's List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd's List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation). IRGC-sourced figures, Iranian state media, and PGSA self-reports do not qualify regardless of the authorization mechanism.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. PGSA addendum (Judge, 2026-05-19): third-country vessels transiting under Iran's PGSA toll regime count ONLY IF ≥2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd's List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls; PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded. IRGC-authorization addendum (Judge, 2026-05-25): all transits authorized by IRGC as gating entity are excluded from resolution counting unless independently confirmed by Lloyd's List Intelligence, Windward, USNI News, UNCTAD, or equivalent non-state maritime intelligence. The exclusion is source-based, not authorization-type-based: an IRGC-coordinated transit independently confirmed by a qualifying source COUNTS.
